Done — one execution, no failures.

**Approach:** a ~50-line script over `safetensors` (`out/T1/solution.py`). It matches whole blocks with `^gpt_neox\.layers\.(\d+)\.(.+)$`, skips blocks 2/6/10/14, and writes survivors into a *fresh* dict under their new indices — so the collision hazard can't occur, and a duplicate destination key would abort anyway.

**Checks, all run before anything is written (exit 1 otherwise):** input has 244 tensors; no destination key written twice; no tensors of blocks 12–15; exactly 12 `attention.query_key_value.weight` matches; indices exactly 0..11; output exactly 184 tensors.

**Verified independently afterwards:** all 12 old→new block mappings are bit-exact with identical shapes/dtypes (spot-checked across weights, biases, and the `attention.bias` / `inv_freq` buffers), and the 4 non-block tensors are unchanged.

I skipped mergekit (passthrough slicing wants contiguous ranges and would force a full transformers re-export) and torch-state-bridge (would still leave saving and validation to me); `out/T1/REPORT.md` records that reasoning along with the rest of the self-report fields.
